Roofing in Haslet, Texas

Haslet is small, but its rule book for roofers is specific: a permit to replace a roof and a yearly city registration backed by insurance. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent roofer that takes Haslet calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Haslet roofer rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Haslet

A railroad village in the middle of Alliance

Roofing in Haslet, TX happens in a town of about two thousand people that sits beside one of the biggest logistics hubs in North Texas. The 2020 census counted 1,952 residents.

Haslet's roots go back to the 1880s. Settlers were in the area by about 1880, and a community took shape after the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe Railway laid track through in 1883. For most of the next century it stayed tiny.

The change came from next door. AllianceTexas has been under development since 1989 around Fort Worth Alliance Airport, which its developer bills as the world's first purely industrial airport. Distribution and logistics buildings spread across the Alliance area, and new subdivisions followed the jobs. So a Haslet roofing call can be about an older house, a newer one in a subdivision, or a very large flat roof.

Haslet's rules for roofers, in order

  1. Register with the city. Every contractor and builder that applies for a permit must be registered with Haslet before any permit is issued.
  2. Carry the insurance. Registration asks for proof of insurance of at least $1,000,000, with the City of Haslet named as certificate holder, plus a photo ID and any state licenses that apply.
  3. Renew yearly. Registration has to be renewed every year, so last year's paperwork is not enough.
  4. Pull the permit. The city lists replacing a roof among the jobs that need a permit, filed through its permit portal or the building services office at 1090 Schoolhouse Road.
  5. Pass inspection. The building department inspects permitted work. Ask the roofer to share the result.

Because registration lapses each year, a roofer that worked in Haslet two summers ago may not be registered today. Ask, and if the answer is vague, call the building services office before anyone tears off a shingle.

That $1 million certificate is the same document you should ask a roofer to send you directly from its insurer. If a company is registered in Haslet this year, it has already produced one for the city.

Kinds of roofing work Haslet calls involve

Full replacements on homes, damage after a spring storm, and roofs over commercial and warehouse buildings are the jobs this town's mix of buildings brings.

What to ask a roofer working in Haslet

  • Is your City of Haslet registration current for this year?
  • Will your insurer send me the same liability certificate you filed with the city?
  • Will you pull the roof permit, and when should I expect the inspection?
  • For a newer home: is the builder's or the manufacturer's warranty still active, and will this work affect it?
  • For a business or warehouse roof: what membrane or metal system is there now, and what does repair versus replacement look like?

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

When storms reach the north edge of Tarrant County

Haslet gets the same spring hail and wind that sweep across the rest of Tarrant County. After a storm, keep off the roof, look from the yard for loose shingles or debris, and photograph what you see inside and out. Call your insurance company to ask about your wind and hail deductible before you decide on a claim. Know which utility serves your address: parts of Haslet are on Oncor and parts on Tri-County Electric Cooperative.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or Tri-County Electric Cooperative, whichever serves your address, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Haslet roofing questions

Is a city permit part of a Haslet TX re-roof?

It is. The City of Haslet lists replacing a roof among the improvements that need a building permit, and its building department handles the permit and the inspections. Applications go through the city's permit portal or the building services office at 1090 Schoolhouse Road, Suite 300. Ask your roofer to apply in its own name and send you the permit number.

What paperwork does Haslet want from a roofing contractor?

Haslet says every contractor and builder applying for a permit must be registered with the city first, and registration must be renewed every year. The application asks for state licenses where they apply, a photo ID, and proof of insurance of at least $1,000,000 with the City of Haslet named as certificate holder. Roofers in Texas hold no state license, which leaves the insurance proof and the ID as the heart of a roofer's file.

Who is my electric provider in Haslet if a storm brings down a line?

It depends on the address. Tri-County Electric Cooperative lists Haslet in its service area, and a City of Haslet utility filing shows some city facilities on Oncor and one on Tri-County, so both serve parts of town. Check your electric bill now so you know whom to call. If a line is down, keep everyone back from it and phone 911 when someone could get hurt.

How does the free roofing line work for Haslet?

An automated assistant answers any time, takes a short description of the roof trouble and the location, then connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Haslet jobs. That company inspects, quotes and works directly with you. See how it works for the details, including the referral fee companies may pay the line.
